newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sumitomo Metal to raise price of China-bound steel.
newsitem.headline: Sumitomo Metal to raise price of China-bound steel.

text.p: Sumitomo Metal Industries said on Monday it had agreed with China to increase the price of its steel products bound for the country by about five percent.

Sumitomo Metal, one of Japan's five major steel makers, said China National Metals & Minerals Import & Export Corp had accepted a price increase for Sumitomo's steel products to be shipped from August 1997 to January 1998.

Sumitomo Metal said the five percent price rise will effect hot-rolled sheets, steel rods, galvanised steel sheets and thick steel sheets, while the price of other steel products will post smaller increases.
The company said the shipment volume for the August-January period was expected to be larger than the preceding February 1997 to July 1997 period. It did not give specifics.

Nippon Steel Corp, NKK Corp, Kobe Steel Ltd said last Thursday they had separately agreed with China National Metals to raise their China-bound steel prices by about five percent, and less than that for other products.
Kawasaki Steel Corp is still in talks with China over its steel prices, a company spokesman said on Monday.
